1	# Paravoxia — orchestration & token discipline
2	
3	Fable weekly limits are the binding constraint; most spend is long-context
4	cache reads, not output. Every session in this repo follows these rules.
5	
6	## Model tiering (frontmatter already set — don't override upward casually)
7	
8	- **fable (inherit)**: `chapter-director`, `score-director`,
9	  `cinematography-director`, `story-alignment-judge`,
10	  `scene-cohesion-judge` — creative build and taste-critical judgment only.
11	- **opus**: `story-naive-reader`, `story-canon-auditor`, `story-verifier`,
12	  `scene-naive-viewer`, `cinematography-continuity-auditor`,
13	  `score-continuity-auditor`, `player-experience-auditor` — blind reading,
14	  auditing, and mechanical verification.
15	- Any ad-hoc Explore/general-purpose agent for searching, doc-reading, log
16	  triage, or probe-running: pass `model: "opus"` (or `"haiku"` for trivial
17	  greps). A mechanical subagent must never inherit fable.
18	
19	## Main-session context hygiene
20	
21	- Stay an orchestrator. Don't pull the design corpus (~65k tokens:
22	  `PARAVOXIA_PROGRESSION.md`, `PARAVOXIA_CH4_PLAN.md`, `main/STORY.md`) into
23	  the main context unless doing the creative work directly here — delegate
24	  reading to a subagent and keep only its conclusions.
25	- Verification (movie probes, screenshot strips, `npm run verify`) goes to
26	  `story-verifier`, not inline Bash loops. Run dev servers and long probes in
27	  the background; read back tails, never full logs.
28	- Guided-play changes require both the verifier's objective/marker/feedback
29	  lifecycle proof and a fresh read-only `player-experience-auditor` report.
30	  Neither role patches or substitutes for a creative director.
31	- After finishing a chapter or review, remind the owner to `/clear` before the
32	  next task; suggest `/compact` before starting a long build phase when
33	  context is already large.
34	
35	## This machine runs concurrent sessions
36	
37	Other agents and the owner work in this repo at the same time. Two incidents in
38	one session on 2026-09-04:
39	
40	- A parallel refactor of `main/src/utils/fauna*.ts` landed mid-`verify` and made
41	  it fail on files the running session had never touched. **Before treating a
42	  gate failure as yours, check `ls -l` timestamps against your last edit.** Do
43	  not "fix" a module someone is actively splitting — you will collide with work
44	  whose destination only they know.
45	- A probe pointed at `127.0.0.1:5199` measured a DIFFERENT PROJECT after that
46	  port was taken over. It returned 200 and rendered a real app, so nothing
47	  looked wrong. **Probes must verify identity, not liveness** — check for
48	  `<title>Paravoxia</title>` before trusting a measurement. `npm run
49	  verify:visual` picks a free port and does this check; copy that pattern.
50	
51	`npm run dev` fails here with `ENOSPC: System limit for number of file watchers
52	reached` (the `captures/` tree is enormous). Use `npm run build` plus
53	`npx vite preview`.
54	
55	Two more harness traps, both hit on 2026-09-04:
56	
57	- **A background shell that waits with `until ! pgrep -f "<name>"` waits forever**,
58	  because the pattern matches the waiting shell's own command line. Use the
59	  bracket trick — `pgrep -f "[n]ame"` — or run dependent steps sequentially in
60	  one shell instead of polling.
61	- **Probes must own their server's lifetime.** Nine orphaned `vite preview`
62	  processes were left behind by probes that crashed. `tools/lib/previewServer.mjs`
63	  now kills the child on exit/signal; use it rather than spawning a preview by
64	  hand. Its `assertHardwareGl` check is also mandatory: without `--use-gl=angle`
65	  headless Chromium here silently used SwiftShader and a boot profile showed a
66	  20-second stall that the real GPU never produces.
67	- **Probe switches** (players never set these): `?worldprep=sync` forces the legacy
68	  synchronous world generation; `?beatregistry=off` serves the legacy story tables
69	  instead of beat contracts. Both exist so a baseline and a candidate come from ONE build.
70	- **Edit-then-measure ordering.** A build started 27 seconds after a source edit
71	  contains that edit. Capture a baseline BEFORE changing the code path it
72	  measures, or use the same-build A/B switches (`?worldprep=sync`,
73	  `?beatregistry=off`) so baseline and candidate come from one build.
74	
75	## Creative triad
76	
77	For any new scene, awakening, substantial cutscene recut, or audiovisual
78	polish pass, invoke the `creative-triad` skill. The Chapter, Score, and
79	Cinematography directors are peers. They communicate through the run's scene
80	contract and structured director notes; they do not race edits in shared
81	timeline files or approve their own implementation.
82	
83	Chapter, Score, and Cinematography are exactly the three peer creative
84	directors. Auditors, verifiers, judges, and integration engineers provide
85	checks, evidence, and repair routing; they never become a fourth creative lane.
86	
87	Durable contracts live in:
88	
89	- `PARAVOXIA_CREATIVE_COUNCIL.md`
90	- `main/CINEMATOGRAPHY.md`
91	- `main/src/story/ux/README.md` (the executable player-guidance context
92	  contract for objective, marker, HUD, and feedback lifecycles)
93	- `docs/architecture/workflow-orchestration/examples/paravoxia-creative-triad.workflow.json`
94	- `.codex/production-runs/_template/`
95	
96	## Story scope
97	
98	Post-arrival story work is **authorized**. The owner lifted the post-arrival
99	gate on 2026-07-28 (recorded at the top of `PARAVOXIA_DEMO_FOUNDATION_PLAN.md`):
100	story beyond `ch9-hearth` may be designed, built, and registered, including the
101	space-station chapter. Do not refuse or defer this work on the basis of an
102	older freeze — earlier revisions of this file carried one, and it expired.
103	
104	What still applies:
105	
106	- **Creative-Triad and registry gates are the remaining barrier** between a new
107	  chapter and the runtime. Route the work through them; do not route around.
108	- **Sequencing is owner-directed: do not rush to the station.** Making the
109	  existing story enjoyable comes first, and the need to leave must emerge from
110	  play rather than from a new content hook.
111	- **The demo's release surface is unchanged** — it still stops at
112	  `ch4-arrival`, and publishing remains a separate decision. Building past it
113	  is allowed; shipping it in the demo is not implied.
114	- **Shipped copy and audio remain protected baselines.** Changing a protected
115	  audio/runtime path is still a contracted change, not an incidental one.
116	- **"Anchorage" is retired as a name.** The location is the **space station**.
